Likely within the foreseeable future to become threatened with extinction (Group 2)
Establishes a new group of animals which are threatened within the foreseeable future with becoming endangered over all or a significant portion of their range. Sec. 2(c)(1)
No change. Sec. 2(c)(1)
Requests for change in classification of a species
Any interested person with substantial evidence may request the Secretary to review any listed species or subspecies. Sec. 3(a)
Any interested person with substantial evidence may petition the Secretary to review any listed or unlisted species or subspecies. Sec. 2(c)(2)

Group 1
The 1969 Act provides no Federal authority to regulate the taking of endangered native animals. (Present authority to regulate taking on Federal lands is because they are wildlife and not because they are endangered.)
Would provide Federal penalties for violation of the Act involving unlawful taking, causing to be taken, shipping, carrying or receiving in interstate commerce any endangered animal of Group 1. Sec. 5(a)(1)
Would provide penalties for violation by any person subject to jurisdiction of U.S. to take, cause to be taken or ship, carry, or receive in interstate commerce any animal of Group 1. Sec. 4(a)

Delegation of regulatory authority to the State
Secretary may delegate to a State the authority to regulate the taking by any person of an endangered species when the Secretary determines that that State maintains an active program to manage and protect such endangered species in accordance with criteria issued by the Secretary.

Sec. 6(b)
Provisions of Sec. 4(a) and (b) may be suspended in any State which has entered into and, in the Secretary's judgment carries out an active program to manage and protect endangered species including enactment and enforcement of adequate State laws. Sec. 5(c)

Sec. 2
Provides penalties for any person convicted of importing into or exporting from the U.S. or causing such acts to occur regarding species or subspecies of Group 1. Sec. 5(a)(1)
Would make unlawful for any person subject to the juris-diction of the U.S. regarding any species or subspecies of Group . or to engage in foreign commerce in any way regarding such animals. Sec. 4(a)
Group 2
Secretary authorized to regulate importation into or export from the U.S. any species or subspecies of Group 2. Sec. 5(b)
Secretary authorized to issue regulations making unlawful any act he deems adviseable for the preservation of a Group 2 species or subspecies.

Sec. 4(b)
Protection of endangered species or subspecies inhabiting international waters.
Group 1
No protection provided.
Provides for punishment of any person who takes on the high seas any species or subspecies of Group 1. Sec. 5(a)(1)
Makes unlawful for any person subject to the jurisdiction of the U.S. to take on the high seas any species or subspecies of Group 1. Sec. 4(a)
Group 2
Provides for punishment of any person who violates regulations issued by the Secretary for the conservation, protection, restoration and propagation of any Group 2 endangered species Such regulations may or may not includes ban on importation. Sec. 5(b)
No change. Sec. 4(b)
Exemptions to prohibitions
Special permit for desirable purposes.
Secretary may permit importation of a listed species for zoological, educational or scientific purposes and for captive propagation for preservation of the species.

Sec. 3(c)
Secretary may permit transportation, importation or taking of a Group 1 endangered species for zoological, educational, or scientific purposes and captive propagation for preservation of the species. Sec. 6(a)
Secretary may permit any action regarding a Group 1 or 2 endangered species when that act is for zoological, education, or scientific purposes to enhance survival of such species. Sec. 5(a)
